subject: FinApps SLA: phased uptime offsets and invoice-credit schedule
messages:
From: Elsa Hart <elsa.hart@finapps.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial SLA proposal for FinApps - service credit phasing & offset ask

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week — we liked the latency profile and the regional routing options. Procurement & legal asked me to share FinApps' preferred SLA ask so we can see where there’s alignment before a legal redline. Attached is our short request doc (FinApps_SLA_Request_v1.pdf). Key points: 

- Uptime baseline: we need a documented monthly availability floor of 99.95% for hosted inference.
- Monthly remedy: automatic pro-rata service credit calculated on impacted usage hours for any month where availability falls below the floor.
- Credit cap phasing: to protect our launch we’re proposing a time-phased cap — 25% of monthly invoice in months 1–3, 40% in months 4–12.
- Invoice offset: FinApps requests the right to temporarily withhold payment for the portion of the invoice equivalent to pending credits until root-cause and remediation are confirmed (we would release after agreed remediation window).
- Maintenance carveouts: limited scheduled maintenance is ok but emergency events should be narrowly defined.
- Latency SLOs: 95th pctile inference latencies for interactive routes should be documented; major degradations to be eligible for credits.

We know some of this is aggressive. Our objective is predictable risk accounting for our finance team while we migrate production traffic. Can you confirm Redwood’s typical baseline and whether you can accept phased caps and the invoice-offset carve?

If helpful, I can set a 30-minute call with our legal & procurement on Thursday afternoon.

Best,
Elsa
Procurement Lead, FinApps
elsa.hart@finapps.com
Procurement: procure@finapps.com

Attachment: FinApps_SLA_Request_v1.pdf (summary of asks)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Elsa Hart <elsa.hart@finapps.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial SLA proposal for FinApps - service credit phasing & offset ask

Hi Elsa — thanks for sending this over and for the clear summary. Short answers up front: Redwood’s hosted baseline for enterprise plans is typically 99.95% monthly availability for production routes, and we do support pro-rata monthly credits when the SLA floor is missed.

A few notes on the specific asks: 
- Phased caps: we’re open to a phased credit-cap approach for the first year, but our standard is to cap monthly credits at a percentage of that month’s invoice (we typically see 10–20%).
- Invoice withholding: we prefer credits applied on the invoice rather than withholding cash; withholding creates collection and cashflow impacts for us and complicates recovery timelines. We can agree to accelerated credit issuance and a short claims window instead.
- Maintenance carveouts: agreed — we’ll list scheduled maintenance windows and require advance notice. Emergency events will require specific qualification (e.g., provider-side infrastructure failures).
- Latency SLOs: we can add a 95th percentile latency SLO for interactive routes; we’ll need concrete traffic profiles to quantify when degradations qualify for credits.

I attached an outline (SLA_Outline_Redwood_v1.pdf) that sketches our counterproposal: 99.95% baseline; rolling 30-day window to submit credit claims; initial monthly credit cap of 15% for months 1–3, 25% months 4–12, and standard 20% moving forward (we can flip those numbers based on volume). We propose no invoice withholding, but we’ll include an escalation path that allows expedited credit processing if there’s clear demonstrated impact.

Can we do Thursday 3pm PT for a quick call? If that works, I’ll invite product and our security rep to answer any profile/latency questions.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Commercial Manager, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Attachment: SLA_Outline_Redwood_v1.pdf

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2027 09:04:00 -07:00
Subject: FW: FinApps SLA ask — recommendation

Marcus / Lauren,

Forwarding FinApps' initial asks (below) and my suggested negotiation positions. High-level: they want 99.95% plus a time-phased credit cap and the right to withhold invoices tied to pending credits. They also want latency SLOs called out.

Recommendations (commercial):
- Keep baseline at 99.95% (we can accept).
- Counter their phasing request: offer 15% cap months 1–3, 25% months 4–12, then revert to a standard 20% thereafter. This balances their launch protection and our exposure.
- Reject invoice withholding — propose explicit credit issuance within the next billing cycle + expedited review path for verified incidents.
- Add a 30-day claim submission window and clear RCA timelines (30/60 escalation ladder).
- Latency: accept a documented 95th percentile SLO for named interactive routes; require FinApps to provide baseline P95 traffic samples to qualify incidents.

Operational asks for product/ops: if we accept the phased caps, we need billing to allow pro-rata credits and product to enable per-route latency telemetry sharing (redwood internal link above). Also want a legal team check on our language to avoid open-ended "emergency" carveouts.

Please advise if you want to push the initial cap lower (10%) for the first quarter or if legal is comfortable with our proposed claim windows. If you sign off, I’ll send the updated outline and schedule the Thursday 3pm PT call.

Thanks,
Kim

Hi Kim,

Thanks for the quick response and for the proposed outline — I reviewed the PDF and shared with our legal team. A couple of quick points from our side: 

- We’re comfortable dropping the invoice withholding if Redwood will commit to a guaranteed credit posting within the next billing cycle (we need a timeline we can show our finance team).
- FinApps would like the initial cap to be 25% for months 1–3 if possible; we can trade a slightly higher cap for a guaranteed remediation SLA (defined RCAs and target mitigation windows).
- On latency: we’ll provide P95 traffic traces for a 7-day steady-state window so your team can calibrate the SLO.

If you can confirm guaranteed credit issuance (e.g., posted to next invoice within 30 days of claim approval) and we get the remediation SLAs in language, I think we can move to a redline. Please send the revised outline and a DocuSign-friendly version of the coverage table.

Booking the Thursday 3pm PT slot now. I’ll invite legal and finance.

Best,
Elsa
